title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft flag Australian copyright barriers to AI training
key_facts: MLex headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft flag Australian copyright barriers to AI training.
Hearing on 6 Oct 2026 in Sydney (Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence); hearings continue to 9 Oct; final report due 30 Nov.
ARIA/PPCA chief Annabelle Herd warned that weakening copyright to attract OpenAI and Anthropic could make Australia the 'Trojan horse for Big AI' and urged licensing deals.
Anthropic's Jeffrey Bleich said obtaining individual licences for training material is technically impossible and hosting training could give Australia influence.
ABC's Kate Gilchrist opposed an opt-out system.
In October 2025 the government ruled out a broad text-and-data-mining exception; Attorney-General Michelle Rowland prefers voluntary licensing.
quote_evidence: Australia’s music industry has warned lawmakers that weakening copyright protections to attract OpenAI and Anthropic could allow technology companies to train artificial intelligence models on copyrighted works without permission.
He argued that obtaining individual licenses for the enormous volume of material used in model training was technically impossible.
why_it_matters_hint: A live fight over who pays for the material that trains AI.
notes: Desk-built entry: MLex is paywalled (headline only, so the Google and Microsoft part rests on that headline alone); facts read at Law Commentary, which reports the 6 Oct 2026 hearing of the Joint Select Committee on AI. Law Commentary names OpenAI and Anthropic but not Google or Microsoft. Stale: event before 8 Oct 2026. Follow-up of our 6 Oct 2026 edition (Forbes Australia item on Anthropic and the AI Safety Institute).
